key_insight: PORTER represents EHR events using language descriptions plus numeric handling, allowing a single model to work across changing vocabularies without losing performance.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce the need for vocabulary harmonization across hospitals and support more portable EHR prediction models.
method: Freezes a text encoder to ground event meaning in language descriptions.
Adds a dedicated pathway for numeric values in clinical events.
Uses an autoregressively pretrained temporal backbone to model patient timelines.
evidence_signal: Across 74 pediatric prediction tasks, PORTER matched a fixed-vocabulary model in mean AUROC and recovered 97.1% of target-vocabulary performance when transferred without retraining; on MIMIC it outperformed a fixed-vocabulary model that lost 69% of events to unseen tokens.
watch_item: Performance may still depend on how well event descriptions are written and mapped, so deployment will need careful validation across sites and pipelines.
paper_title: PORTER: Language-Grounded Event Representations for Portable Structured EHR Foundation Models
